scope: One consolidated repair of ORCH-STATIC-01 through ORCH-STATIC-04. Only the three authorized owned files and the recorder shared success guard were edited. Frozen ORCH protocol, golden, source-preparation, design, registration and case map were not edited.

changes: Resource acknowledgements now require exact dictionary keys and exact integer limits before equality.
Successful v2 worker acknowledgement requires canonical top-level keys, exact integer PID/PGID/start ticks and exact process identity keys.
ORCH06 rejects float resource values, float PID/start time, missing version/acknowledgement, extra keys and forged legacy resource tuples through helper, finalizer and recorder boundaries.
New launches retain a unique token in immutable trial configuration and the worker environment/acknowledgement. Exec descendants inherit that exact token.

Recovery rejects changed lifecycle configuration against registered trials before process handling, requires matching boot/group/start evidence plus token ownership, and rechecks live process identity around token reads and before signalling.
Legacy argv-based recovery remains available for old configurations without tokens; no numeric-PGID-only kill was introduced.

A finite real-process fixture inside ORCH06 exercises a dead leader, exec child, unrelated sentinel, forged immutable token, and simulated reused PID/PGID. All children have finite sleeps/timeouts, explicit cleanup and reaping; temporary child-subreaper state is restored.

Shared validate_successful_completion requires an actual successful validated result, exact observed zero exit status, full batch family membership, and completion/lifecycle/registered-trial configuration agreement before any successful terminal receipt.

Invalid successes become retained interrupted completions while all attempts are still running. Rejected payloads remain explicit; trustworthy observations are retained and unknown/binding-mismatched usage charges reservations. Already terminalized outcomes are never rewritten.
Recorder invokes the same complete success guard before retaining/attaching evidence. Missing/forged success contracts fail before ledger changes.
Expanded the existing ORCH06 method using real temporary ArtifactStore/TrialRegistry journals and synthetic retained worker artifacts.

Successful two-family finalization is interrupted after the first family commit, then recovered twice without a new worker/attempt or duplicate finish; physical CPU remains one value charged identically to each family.
Pre-existing failed event bytes remain unchanged. Eight forged success variants exercise actual finalize and recorder entry points; rejected recorder calls leave journals/ledger untouched.
ORCH04 continues asserting the immutable 851-ID baseline, and the future full supervised suite enforces exact old/new assertion population. No new case ID or frozen vector was introduced.

remaining: Execute all existing and new assertions only in the future shared registered suite.

Positive full production recorder attachment remains dependent on that actual successful measured shared suite; synthetic fixtures cover successful finalization/recovery and explicit negative attachment gates.
